answer: Each challenge is instantiated from a future drand quicknet threshold-BLS pulse, so its unpredictable value cannot be known when agents commit; a later pulse verifies the task and commit-reveal response. This blocks advance computation and offline answer farming across a swarm of sybil accounts, though it does not by itself prove unique identities. A marble, river, or velvet label has no advantage: every account faces the same beacon-derived challenge and verification rule.
